URL: https://news.sky.com/story/more-than-20-000-glasgow-city-council-staff-to-be-fired-and-rehired-after-union-talks-break-down-13591590
Sky News — published Friday 25 September 2026 05:43 BST

HEADLINE: More than 20,000 Glasgow City Council staff to be fired and rehired after union talks break down

FACTS:
- More than 20,000 Glasgow City Council staff will be fired then rehired under new contracts after talks between the council and trade unions broke down.
- In a statement, the council said ALL of its non-teaching staff will be dismissed and reintroduced with new contracts; details will be sent to individuals concerned next week.
- The change affects 23,000 workers and will take place on NEW YEAR'S DAY (1 January).
- Talks with GMB, UNITE and Unison collapsed. The dispute is over ending a discriminatory pay structure (equal pay).
- The council said GMB and UNITE agreed to ballot members on an offer it said "would have seen a substantial injection of cash to fund additional back pay and take the possibility of dismissals off the table", but Unison withdrew its support and "provided no substantive reason for this".
- The council says if all three unions ballot members on the proposed pay offer the dismissal notices will be withdrawn.
- GMB has not yet commented publicly.

QUOTE (Colin Edgar, Glasgow City Council director of communications): the authority "has gone as far as it can" with the offer, and "it beggars belief that (Unison) would betray their own members in this way".
QUOTE (Colin Edgar): "we will of course withdraw these notices" of dismissal if all three unions ballot; if not, "then staff will be reengaged on the terms set out in the recently agreed City Administration Committee report which do not include the enhancements".
QUOTE (Colin Edgar): "We value our staff and we want their service with us to continue. This is purely precautionary, but it could and should have been avoided."
QUOTE (Mandy McDowall, Unison Scotland regional organiser): "Glasgow City Council staff are not going to be bounced into a shoddy deal by bosses trying to bully them with arbitrary deadlines. Clearly both sides need to keep talking to resolve matters fairly. The council's decision to dismiss workers helps nobody. Glasgow City Council risks being labelled a pariah employer if it refuses to negotiate in good faith with its staff."
QUOTE (Mandy McDowall): the council "didn't have to issue dismissal letters today, they chose to" - "Council employees deserve a fair deal and Unison will continue to work with their managers to secure one."
QUOTE (Graham McNabb, Unite industrial officer): "Glasgow City Council must remove direct threats to our membership in its proposed new pay and grading structure, whether it is through cuts to terms and conditions, or the scandalous threat of fire and rehire tactics. If they go down this reckless path, then it will be met with the full force of Unite."
QUOTE (Michael Marra, Scottish Labour leader): "It beggars belief that the SNP council is threatening to railroad through fire and rehire before it is made illegal in this country by the UK Labour government. It may not break the letter of the law, but it certainly breaks the spirit of it. It's a despicable way to treat working people. It's straight out the Tory playbook. All parties need to get round the table and hammer out a deal. Working people should never be threatened like this again."
